headline: Where Does AI Actually Add Value?
thesis: From Educause's No. 1 priority to a Maryland trial with 15% uptake, higher ed and K-12 are both asking AI to prove its worth.
summary: This week's coverage converges on one question: where does AI add real value? Educause's 2027 Top 10 ranks it first for the first time, provosts use AI personally but few institutions have a strategy, and a University of Maryland trial of its own study assistant was inconclusive. In K-12, the Chan Zuckerberg-backed Learning Commons launched an open platform with 70+ partners, while Brookings and EdSurge voices debate caution versus panic. Ed-Fi's state stories and post-ESSER tutoring data show that durable infrastructure and funding choices matter as much as the tools.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · OCTOBER 19, 2026 · Search-based research; several sites had no indexed items dated today, so evergreen and recent items are included and noted.

themes.title: Student Protection & Trust

themes.title: Teachers, Faculty & Students

themes.title: Funding & Infrastructure
